code: # Single-channel Poisson deconvolution: shifted copies of a known PSF. single <- simul(method=2, n=500, p=500, s=.1, seed=2) fit_single <- L0glm.fit(single$X, single$y, family=poisson(identity),   lambda="gic", nonnegative=TRUE, relaxed=TRUE, parallelize=FALSE) L0glm.metrics(fit_single, beta_true=single$beta_true)[   c("gic", "TP", "FP", "FN", "TN", "F1_score", "MCC")]  old_par <- par(no.readonly=TRUE) par(mfrow=c(1, 1), mgp=c(2, .7, 0)) # The default PSF has peak one. Scale both spike trains by the same PSF peak # to display them in signal units; negative values indicate mirroring only. spike_scale <- max(single$X) beta_single <- as.numeric(coef(fit_single)) mu_single <- as.numeric(fitted(fit_single)) height <- max(as.numeric(single$y), as.numeric(single$y_true), mu_single,   as.numeric(single$beta_true)*spike_scale, beta_single*spike_scale) plot(single$x, single$y, type="l", col="grey65", ylim=c(-1, 1)*height*1.15,   xlab="Time", ylab="Signal / spike height (fit mirrored)",   main="Single-channel Poisson deconvolution") abline(h=0, col="grey75", lty=3) lines(single$x, single$y_true, col="grey30", lty=2) segments(single$x_beta, 0, single$x_beta,   as.numeric(single$beta_true)*spike_scale, col="navy") lines(single$x, -mu_single, col="orange", lwd=1.5) segments(single$x_beta, 0, single$x_beta, -beta_single*spike_scale, col="red") legend("topright", c("Observed signal", "True signal", "True spikes",   "Fitted signal (mirrored)", "Fitted spikes (mirrored)"),   col=c("grey65", "grey30", "navy", "orange", "red"),   lty=c(1, 2, 1, 1, 1), bty="n", cex=.75)  # Multichannel Poisson deconvolution: select rows shared across channels. # Retain every mass channel generated by the simulation. multi <- simul(method=4, n=500, p=500, s=.05, seed=2) fit_multi <- L0glm.fit(multi$X, multi$y, family=poisson(identity),   lambda="gic", nonnegative=TRUE, grouped=TRUE, relaxed=TRUE,   parallelize=FALSE) L0glm.metrics(fit_multi, beta_true=multi$beta_true)[   c("gic", "TP", "FP", "FN", "TN", "F1_score", "MCC",     "within_row_F1_score", "within_row_MCC")] # The within-row scores assess channel sparsity among correctly recovered rows. dim(coef(fit_multi))                  # original predictors by response channels par(mfrow=c(2, 1)) plotmat(multi$beta_true, xlab="Spike location", ylab="Channel",   main="True multichannel coefficients") plotmat(coef(fit_multi), xlab="Spike location", ylab="Channel",   main="Estimated multichannel coefficients") par(old_par)  # High-dimensional Gaussian regression with positive and negative effects. # Run manually: the dense design alone occupies about 4 GB. if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ n <- 500L p <- 1000000L set.seed(123) X_hd <- matrix(rnorm(n*p), n, p) support <- sample.int(p, 60L) beta_hd <- numeric(p) beta_hd[support] <- runif(60L, -.8, .8) mean_hd <- as.numeric(X_hd[, support, drop=FALSE] %*% beta_hd[support]) set.seed(1) y_hd <- mean_hd + rnorm(n)  # screen="auto" activates ISIS for this ultra-wide design. Screened fits # default to the original-p GIC preset and a relaxed refit. # Screening threads are independent of BLAS threads (nthreads). system.time(fit_hd <- L0glm.fit(X_hd, y_hd, screen.nthreads=8, nthreads=1)) fit_hd$screening[c("method", "screen_size", "iterations", "best_iteration", "nthreads")] fit_hd$screening$history L0glm.metrics(fit_hd, beta_true=beta_hd)[   c("gic", "TP", "FP", "FN", "TN", "F1_score", "MCC")] dim(coef(fit_hd))                    # all p rows, including screened-out zeros # Explicit alternatives: screen="SIS", "ISIS", or "none". } # }  # Basic controls: intercept constraints, dispersion and binomial fits. x <- seq(-1, 1, length.out=30) X <- matrix(x, ncol=1)  # Nonnegativity includes the Gaussian intercept. constrained <- L0glm.fit(X, -2+3*x, family=gaussian(),   intercept=TRUE, nonnegative=TRUE, lambda=1e-8,   dispersion=1, parallelize=FALSE) as.numeric(constrained$coefficients)  # Estimate Gaussian variance from an automatic or user-supplied start. set.seed(1) y_gaussian <- 2*x + rnorm(length(x), sd=.5) automatic <- L0glm.fit(X, y_gaussian, family=gaussian(),   lambda="gic", dispersion=NULL, maxit=100, parallelize=FALSE) initialized <- L0glm.fit(X, y_gaussian, family=gaussian(),   lambda="gic", dispersion=-.25, maxit=100, parallelize=FALSE) # dispersion=.25 instead keeps the variance fixed at .25.  # A binomial intercept may remain negative with a nonnegative slope. y <- round(1000*plogis(-2+x))/1000 logistic <- L0glm.fit(X, y, family=binomial(),   weights=rep(1000, length(y)), nonnegative=TRUE,   lambda=1e-8, parallelize=FALSE) as.numeric(logistic$coefficients)  # Gaussian validation-based stopping: keep a separate test set for assessment. set.seed(42) X_validation <- matrix(rnorm(200*40), 200, 40) y_validation <- 3 + 2*X_validation[, 1] - X_validation[, 2] + rnorm(200) train <- 1:120 fit_stopped <- L0glm.fit(X_validation[train, ], y_validation[train],   intercept=TRUE, lambda="gic", relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100,   validation=list(X=X_validation[-train, ], y=y_validation[-train]),   parallelize=FALSE) fit_stopped$validation$selection[c("best_iteration", "iterations", "stopped")]  # Optionally select the ISIS batch on the same validation set. # Omit nsis to keep the GIC-based default batch. fit_batch <- L0glm.fit(X_validation[train, ], y_validation[train],   intercept=TRUE, lambda="gic", screen="ISIS", nsis=c(1, 3, 5, 10),   relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100, validation=list(     X=X_validation[-train, ], y=y_validation[-train], rule="1se"),   parallelize=FALSE) fit_batch$validation[c("selected_start", "selected_nsis", "deviance")] fit_batch$validation$starts # Sparse special families: GIC preset fits, GIC tuning and three-fold CV. if (requireNamespace("mgcv", quietly=TRUE)) {   set.seed(204)   n <- 300L   X_special <- matrix(rnorm(n*20), n, 20)   folds_special <- sample(rep(1:3, length.out=n))   family_par <- par(mgp=c(2, .7, 0))    # Negative binomial: two nonzero slopes among 20 predictors.   mu_nb <- exp(.4 + .8*X_special[, 1] - .6*X_special[, 2])   y_nb <- rnbinom(n, mu=mu_nb, size=2)   # nb() estimates theta; nb(theta=2) would keep it fixed at two.   nb_fit <- L0glm.fit(X_special, y_nb, family=mgcv::nb(),     intercept=TRUE, lambda="gic", relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100, tol=1e-8)   nb_fit$theta   coef(nb_fit)   nb_gic <- L0glm.tune(X_special, y_nb, family=mgcv::nb(),     intercept=TRUE, tune="gic", nlambda=5,     relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100, tol=1e-8)   nb_cv <- L0glm.tune(X_special, y_nb, family=mgcv::nb(),     intercept=TRUE, tune="cv", nlambda=5, nfolds=3, foldid=folds_special,     relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100, tol=1e-8)   c(GIC=nb_gic$lambda_best, CV=nb_cv$lambda_best, CV_1se=nb_cv$lambda_1se)   predict(nb_cv$fit_1se, X_special[1:5, , drop=FALSE], type="response")    # Three-category multinomial: only two predictor rows affect probabilities.   eta <- cbind(0, .9*X_special[, 1] - .7*X_special[, 2],     -.8*X_special[, 1] + .6*X_special[, 2])   probabilities <- exp(eta - apply(eta, 1, max))   probabilities <- probabilities/rowSums(probabilities)   y_multinomial <- factor(vapply(seq_len(n), function(i)     sample.int(3, 1, prob=probabilities[i, ]), integer(1)), levels=1:3)   multinomial_fit <- L0glm.fit(X_special, y_multinomial,     family=mgcv::multinom(K=2), lambda="gic", grouped=TRUE,     relaxed=TRUE, maxit=200, tol=1e-8)   coef(multinomial_fit)               # original-scale, zero-sum CLR rows   multinomial_gic <- L0glm.tune(X_special, y_multinomial,     family=mgcv::multinom(K=2), tune="gic", nlambda=5, grouped=TRUE,     relaxed=TRUE, maxit=200, tol=1e-8)   multinomial_cv <- L0glm.tune(X_special, y_multinomial,     family=mgcv::multinom(K=2), tune="cv", nlambda=5,     nfolds=3, foldid=folds_special, grouped=TRUE,     relaxed=TRUE, maxit=200, tol=1e-8)   c(GIC=multinomial_gic$lambda_best, CV=multinomial_cv$lambda_best,     CV_1se=multinomial_cv$lambda_1se)   predict(multinomial_cv$fit_1se, X_special[1:5, , drop=FALSE], type="response")    # Right-censored Cox model: two nonzero log-hazard effects, no intercept.   if (requireNamespace("survival", quietly=TRUE)) {     event_time <- rexp(n, rate=exp(.7*X_special[, 1] - .5*X_special[, 2]))     censor_time <- rexp(n, rate=.4)     y_cox <- survival::Surv(pmin(event_time, censor_time),       event_time <= censor_time)     cox_fit <- L0glm.fit(X_special, y_cox, family=mgcv::cox.ph(),       lambda="gic", relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100, tol=1e-8)     coef(cox_fit)     cox_gic <- L0glm.tune(X_special, y_cox, family=mgcv::cox.ph(),       tune="gic", nlambda=5, relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100, tol=1e-8)     cox_cv <- L0glm.tune(X_special, y_cox, family=mgcv::cox.ph(),       tune="cv", nlambda=5, nfolds=3, foldid=folds_special,       relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100, tol=1e-8)     c(GIC=cox_gic$lambda_best, CV=cox_cv$lambda_best, CV_1se=cox_cv$lambda_1se)     predict(cox_cv$fit_1se, X_special[1:5, , drop=FALSE], type="risk")   }   par(family_par) }

OpenMP is used across outcome channels when available. system.time(fit.mc <- L0nnpois(   sim.pois.mc$X,   sim.pois.mc$y,   lambda = "gic",   grouped = TRUE,   relaxed = TRUE,   parallelize = TRUE,   ncores = round(parallel::detectCores(logical = FALSE)/2) ))  # with n <- p <- 1000 and npeaks <- 100   0.56s with 4 cores on my machine # with n <- p <- 10000 and npeaks <- 1000 9.41s with 4 cores on my machine  dim(fit.mc$coefficients) sum(fit.mc$coefficients != 0)  if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ ## code: set.seed(1) n <- 150; p <- 300 X <- matrix(rnorm(n*p),n,p) beta <- c(1,-1,.8,-.8,rep(0,p-4)) y <- as.numeric(X%*%beta)+rnorm(n) screen <- sis_glm(X,y,nsis=40,return_stats=FALSE) screen$indices threaded <- sis_glm(X,y,nsis=40,return_stats=FALSE,nthreads=4) identical(threaded$indices,screen$indices)  # Independent channels are screened jointly without signed cancellation. multi <- sis_glm(X,cbind(y,-y),nsis=40,return_stats=FALSE) multi$indices  # Conditional screening includes the specified nuisance design. conditional <- sis_glm(X,y,nuisance=cbind(1,X[,1]),nsis=40) head(conditional$stats[conditional$ranking,])  # Offset-based outer ISIS; each candidate fit starts afresh. iterated <- sis_glm(X,y,nsis=40,iterative=TRUE,niter=10,return_stats=FALSE) iterated$history coef(iterated$fit)                 # sparse, all original predictor rows head(predict(iterated$fit,X[1:5,,drop=FALSE]))  # The same full-dimension model through the main fitting interface. fit <- L0glm.fit(X,y,screen="ISIS",nsis=40,screen.maxit=10,screen.nthreads=4) fit$screening$history coef(fit) # screen="auto" (the default) enables ISIS only for ultra-wide eligible designs. # Use screen="none" to fit the full design directly.  if (requireNamespace("mgcv",quietly=TRUE)) {   counts <- rnbinom(n,mu=exp(.5+.4*X[,1]),size=2)   nb <- sis_glm(X,counts,family=mgcv::nb(),nsis=20,return_stats=FALSE)   nb$theta   classes <- factor(sample(letters[1:3],n,TRUE))   multinomial <- sis_glm(X,classes,family=mgcv::multinom(2),                         nsis=20,return_stats=FALSE) } if (requireNamespace("mgcv",quietly=TRUE) && requireNamespace("survival",quietly=TRUE)) {   time <- rexp(n,exp(.5*X[,1]))   outcome <- survival::Surv(pmin(time,2),time<=2)   cox <- sis_glm(Matrix::Matrix(X,sparse=TRUE),outcome,                 family=mgcv::cox.ph(),nsis=20,return_stats=FALSE) }

code: # Sparse Gaussian regression. set.seed(1) X <- matrix(rnorm(360),60,6) truth <- c(2,-1,rep(0,4)) y <- as.numeric(X %*% truth + rnorm(60)) comparison <- sparseglm(X,y,method=c("lasso","relaxed_lasso"),   tune="gic",nlambda=5,beta_true=truth) L0glm.metrics(comparison)[c("method","seconds","gic","adj_R2_weighted","F1_score","MCC")] plot(comparison,which=c(1,2))  # Blurred Poisson spike trains: smaller versions of the single/multichannel # deconvolution benchmarks. MCP and SCAD are omitted because they were slow # on the large deconvolution examples. All times below are measured locally. comparison_methods <- c("L0glm","abess","L0Learn","lasso","relaxed_lasso",                         "adaptive_lasso","adaptive_relaxed_lasso") fields <- c("method","seconds","gic","deviance","adj_R2_weighted","F1_score","MCC")  # Single channel: 50 spikes among 500 candidate locations. single <- simul(method=2,n=500,p=500,s=.1,seed=2) lambda_gic <- log(ncol(single$X))*log(log(nrow(single$X))) comparison_single <- sparseglm(single,family=poisson(identity),   method=comparison_methods,tune="gic",nlambda=10,   nonnegative=TRUE,intercept=FALSE,approximation="wls",   support.size=1:100,lambda=list(L0glm=lambda_gic),   options=list(L0glm=list(relaxed=FALSE),abess=list(warm.start=TRUE))) L0glm.metrics(comparison_single)[fields] plot(comparison_single,which=c(1,2,4,5))  # Multichannel: use 100 time points and six abundant mass channels for speed. multi <- simul(method=4,n=100,p=100,s=.1,seed=2) keep <- head(order(Matrix::colSums(multi$y),decreasing=TRUE),6) for (name in c("y","y_true","beta_true")) multi[[name]] <- multi[[name]][,keep,drop=FALSE] lambda_gic <- log(ncol(multi$X))*log(log(nrow(multi$X))) comparison_multi <- sparseglm(multi,family=poisson(identity),   method=comparison_methods,tune="gic",nlambda=10,   nonnegative=TRUE,intercept=FALSE,approximation="wls_grouped",   support.size=1:20,lambda=list(L0glm=lambda_gic),   options=list(L0glm=list(relaxed=TRUE),abess=list(warm.start=TRUE))) # ABESS and glmnet select rows jointly using Gaussian shared-row-weight WLS; # L0glm fits the exact grouped Poisson model. L0Learn fits channels independently. # GIC, deviance and prediction R-squared always use the original Poisson model.
